newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel sees bond with Turkey against "extremists".
newsitem.headline: Israel sees bond with Turkey against "extremists".

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said after meeting Turkish armed forces chief General Ismail Hakki Karadayi on Thursday the two countries had interest in cooperating against "extremist elements."

Karadayi, on a three-day visit to the Jewish state, met Netanyahu at his office with Israeli army chief Amnon Shahak and the prime minister's military secretary, a statement from Netanyahu's office said.

"We appreciate Turkey and its army and I believe our cooperation is a very important component in securing the aspiration for peace and stability in the Middle East, an area that has many extremist elements," the statement quoted Netanyahu as saying.
"Turkey and Israel have a joint interest in securing stability, peace and moderation in our region."
Accords between their armies and military industries have strengthened ties between Islamist-led but secular Turkey and the Jewish state.

On Wednesday Israel Aircraft Industries received the first of 54 Turkish F-4 Phantom jets under a $600 million deal from 1995 to upgrade the Turkish Air Force's fleet over five years, the company said.
Israel and Turkey also signed an accord allowing Israeli jets train in Turkish airspace.
The accords were condemned by Iran and many Arab states. Ankara's closer links with Israel also drew strong protests from Islamists in Turkey.
But since becoming prime minister eight months ago Turkey's Islamist Welfare Party leader Necmettin Erbakan has toned down his criticism.

The statement from the prime minister's office quoted Karadayi as thanking Netanyahu for the meeting and saying: "The relations between Turkey and Israel have always been good and will be even better in the future.
"There are excellent relations between our armies and our military industries and this visit left me with a very good impression."
